These appeals are filed under Section 74(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 20131 laying a challenge to the Judgment & Award dated 27.09.2023 passed by the Reference Court in LAC Nos.11/2019, 12/2019 and 13/2019, whereunder enhancement of compensation has been accorded.

sentences.text: The above appeals are filed beyond the prescribed period of 60 + 60 = 120 days and there is a delay of 175 days in filing these appeals.
Applications are filed seeking condonation of delay in all these appeals.

Hereinafter referred as "the 2013 Act"
NC: 2024:KHC-D:16000 3. Section 74(1) along with the Proviso thereto (sub-section (2) not being relevant) of the 2013 Act is noticed for ready reference:
"74. Appeal to High Court.
(1) The Requiring Body or any person aggrieved by the Award passed by an Authority under section 69 may file an appeal to the High Court within sixty days from the date of Award:
Provided that the High Court may, if it is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal within the said period, allow it to be filed within a further period not exceeding sixty days."
4. The language of Sub-section (1) of Section 74 and the proviso thereof of the 2013 Act is clear.

Further, a Division Bench of this Court in the case of THE DEPUTY COMMISSIONER AND SPECIAL LAND ACQUISITION OFFICER, BENGALURU VS. M/S. S.V. GLOBAL MILL LIMITED, CHENNAI2, has examined the matter in great detail and held that Section 74 of the 2013 Act is mandatory in nature and an application for condonation of ILR 2020 KAR 1897 NC: 2024:KHC-D:16000 delay beyond the statutorily permissible time limit is not liable to be favourably considered.
